Lina (CSE): OrchIDCo hitting a spike of 429s during onboarding in staging. They spin up a fleet of lambda-style workers that each call sdk.init() at coldstart. Seen ~40% init failures in first minute.
OrchidCo (engineer): repro: deploy 50 workers (concurrent) -> each does sdk.init() -> many get 429 with retry_after small. No token rotation.
Nia (Support): can you paste the exact response body and headers? Are we returning Retry-After?

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limited",
  "message": "preflight limit exceeded",
  "retry_after": 2
}
```
Headers: x-edge-route: /v1/preflight, x-preflight-window: 1s
Devon (Eng): sounds like a preflight stampede + ephemeral token fanout. Quick client-side fixes: 1) stagger init with random jitter, 2) reuse a single token across forks when possible, 3) prefer keepalive / pooled connections.
Ravi (Platform): server-side options: we can temporarily raise their preflight concurrency cap on the edge for a short window, and enable preflight coalescing for their tenant. I can make a 30m override.
Lina (CSE): please do the override while we ask them to patch client. Also note: if this continues into prod they could be flagged for onboarding health.
OrchidCo (engineer): patch idea: add a randomized sleep(0..300ms) before init, enable http2 keepalive, and set sdk.option.connPool=true. Any code sample?
Devon (Eng): sample snippet for their runtime:
```
// warmup-safe init
await sleep(random(0, 300));
const client = new RedwoodSDK({ connPool: true, preflightCoalesceMs: 150, keepAlive: true });
await client.init();
```
And for token refresh splay:
```
// on startup
const token = await fetchToken();
await sleep(random(0, 1000));
shareTokenAcrossWorkers(token);
```
